Reading older documents

Documents of older versions are read into the current model after 155 rules from crates/idml/schema-upgrades.tsv: 54 drop data (with a warning), 78 put elements where they are allowed now, 11 map or complete values and 12 confirm that old values stay valid.

Reading the reports

  • Added items are in the version, not in the one before; removed items the other way round; moved items are no longer allowed where they were but still in the same parent, nested in elements without an identity (a <TextFrame> in <Story> is now in <CharacterStyleRange>; an attribute became a <Properties> element); changed items have a different type, presence or occurrence; restored items were removed earlier and are back.
  • Where versions are missing between two snapshots, a change happened somewhere in between.
  • 6.0 exists only as a single-file schema, which has no designmap and no part roots: those items are first compared from 7.0 on. For everything else it lists exactly what the package schemas do (checked with InDesign 21.5.1.73, generated in both forms).
  • The Rust column names the item of the generated model that represents a schema item today.
  • A renamed item shows as removed and added. Move hints come from the schemas alone; whether InDesign means the same by the new place is a judgement, recorded in crates/idml/schema-upgrades.tsv.
